headline: Two oil tankers explode in Strait of Hormuz amid escalating US-Iran tensions
summary: Two oil tankers reportedly exploded after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guard. This incident further escalates tensions in the strategic waterway.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy reported yesterday that two oil tankers "exploded" after hitting mines. The incident occurred while the vessels were traveling through an "unauthorized route" in the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has previously imposed restrictions on vessels in the strait, attacking ships it claims violate these rules. This is part of its effort to assert control over the waterway and exert pressure on the United States.

Despite the incident, Iran stated its readiness to reopen the strait within two days if the US agrees to its conditions. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei called this a sign of Iran's "good-faith approach."
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump reiterated his threat to resume strikes against Iran. He told a campaign rally that he might have to give Tehran "the hammer" at an unspecified time.
Trump also held discussions with Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu regarding the timing and possibility of escalating combat operations against Iran, according to US media reports.

In a separate development, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Oman’s sultan that the Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry. China is willing to work with Arab nations for lasting peace.

Separately, Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported at least seven people were wounded following Saudi-led coalition air attacks on Yemen’s rebel-controlled Hodeidah governorate. Four were wounded at Ras Isa port and three in an oil company raid.

Esmaeil Baqaei also accused the US of being the "biggest threat" to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, as reported by state broadcaster IRIB. He criticized the IAEA for not condemning alleged US attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities.

headline_marked: [[Four national leaders murdered]] in Dhaka Central Jail on November 3, 1975, amid power struggle
headline: Four national leaders murdered in Dhaka Central Jail on November 3, 1975, amid power struggle
summary: The national tragedy, which saw Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, M Mansur Ali, and AHM Qamaruzzaman killed, occurred during a fierce military power struggle following Bangabandhu's assassination.
details: The execution had already been approved from the highest authority of the country, targeting four of the most important figures in Bangladesh’s history. The location was one of the state’s most heavily guarded institutions – the Dhaka Central Jail.

The victims of this despicable conspiracy were Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, M Mansur Ali, and AHM Qamaruzzaman. These leaders had guided Bangladesh through the darkest days of the Liberation War, held together the government-in-exile in 1971, and steered the struggle for independence.

The national tragedy that unfolded inside the jail in the early hours of November 3, 1975, was not an isolated act of violence. It took place amid a fierce power struggle within the military that followed the assassination of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman on August 15, 1975.

As senior army officers moved to challenge the president’s self-confessed killers, another plot was underway behind prison walls. Nazrul, Tajuddin, Mansur, and Qamaruzzaman had landed in jail on politically motivated charges of corruption under martial law.

According to the full verdict of the Appellate Division delivered on April 30, 2013, a chain of events began unfolding around 3:00am on November 3. The then Inspector General of Prisons, Nuruzzaman Howlader, received several telephone calls from army personnel at the Bangabhaban.

He was instructed to proceed immediately to Dhaka Central Jail, where he and Deputy Inspector General of Prisons Kazi Abdul Awal sat in the office. Sometime later, Captain Moslem Uddin arrived with four armed personnel, asking if the four leaders had been kept separately as instructed.

Offering no explanations, the armed personnel plainly announced that the four men were to be put to death. Nuruzzaman then sought to speak to President Khandaker Mushtaque Ahmed, who instructed him over the phone to let the five army personnel “do whatever they wanted to do”.

The armed men then entered the prison and opened fire on the four leaders. After Fajr prayers, Nuruzzaman learned that another group of armed personnel had arrived to confirm the kills, discovering two leaders were still alive and killing them with bayonets.

Years later, retired Brigadier General M Sakhawat Hussain wrote that the murder of the four leaders in jail “took place with the informed consent of Rashid and Mushtaque.” He recalled that the massacre occurred in the dead of night, coinciding with the counter-coup of November 2-3.

According to Sakhawat, apart from Mushtaque and Rashid, only Major General Khalilur Rahman knew about the jail killings. Moslem claimed he personally killed the imprisoned leaders with a burst of fire from a Sten gun, thus completing one of the most brutal murders in history with state-level consent.
